name: Indegene Limited
tagline: AI-enabled pharma tech and life sciences operating partner to top-20 biopharma companies; revenue growth strong (+30% TTM) but profit growth stalled (-4% TTM), signaling margin compression and operational headwinds; ROCE declined from 37% (FY20) to 19% (FY26)
business_overview: Indegene provides analytics, technology, and commercial/medical/regulatory/safety services to global life sciences and healthcare organizations. Strategic operating partner to the world's top 20 biopharma companies, spanning discovery & evidence, regulatory & compliance, commercial launch, content & engagement, and patient & outcomes. Services delivered through AI-enabled platforms and governed operating models.
fundamentals_table: FY26 Rs 3,510 Cr (+36% YoY); TTM Rs 3,813 Cr (+30% YoY)
FY26 Rs 401 Cr (+20% YoY); TTM Rs 401 Cr (-4% YoY) — profit growth stalled
Rs 144 Cr borrowings (net of cash ~Rs 150 Cr approx low leverage)
FY26 depreciation Rs 126 Cr (elevated), investing for AI platform build-out
P/E ~34.4x; P/B ~4.6x; stock up only 2% in 1 year (underperformer)
fundamentals_narrative: Indegene has delivered 5-year revenue CAGR of 29% (to Rs 3,510 Cr FY26) and 5-year profit CAGR of 23% (to Rs 401 Cr). However, Q1 FY27 showed a critical inflection: revenue +39.7% but profit +0.17% YoY (essentially flat), signaling severe margin compression. TTM profit has contracted to Rs 401 Cr despite TTM revenue reaching Rs 3,813 Cr (+30% YoY), indicating pricing pressure or operational inefficiency. ROCE has deteriorated from 37% (FY20) to 19% (FY26), a 50% decline despite continued capex spending (Rs 126 Cr depreciation FY26, highest in history). Debtor days elevated at 102 (vs 91 in FY24), suggesting longer receivables cycles or weaker customer quality. The company is scaling revenue but losing earnings momentum, a classic sign of commoditization or margin pressure in the BPO/tech services industry.
technical_read: Stock at Rs 594 (Oct 1, 2026), up only 2% in 1 year; lagging Nifty 50 and most IT/services peers. Recent concall (expected Oct 30, 2026 per BSE filing) will be critical to understand the profit margin headwinds. P/E of 34.4x is elevated vs Nifty average but justified if profit growth re-accelerates; currently not justified given TTM profit contraction.
sentiment_summary: IPO (May 2024) at Rs 600 suggested strong pent-up demand for pharma tech exposure. Stock has underperformed since, suggesting market has repriced growth expectations downward as margin pressures became evident.
community_signal: No ValuePickr thread found (web discovery only). Indegene is less discussed than pure-play IT services companies; pharma tech is a niche sector.
bse_notes: No SEBI action or auditor qualification found. ICRA credit rating A (stable) as of 2025.
bull_case: Niche market: top-20 biopharma customer base provides recurring revenue and scale potential
AI platform differentiation: AI-enabled services reduce manual work, improve margins as scale grows
Secular growth: Life sciences digital transformation and regulatory complexity drive enduring demand
IPO catalysts: Platform consolidation, M&A, international expansion opportunities to drive 15-20% CAGR
Low leverage: Debt-free balance sheet provides M&A flexibility and financial stability
bear_case: Margin compression: Q1 FY27 profit essentially flat (+0.17%) despite revenue +39.7%; TTM profit -4% vs revenue +30% is a red flag
Revenue dilution: Growth mix is skewing toward lower-margin services; ASP per client may be declining
ROCE deterioration: From 37% (FY20) to 19% (FY26); company is deploying capital less efficiently
Debtor days extended: 102 days (vs 91 in FY24) suggests weaker customer quality or extended payment terms = working capital headwind
Customer concentration: Top-20 biopharma customer base means high concentration risk if major client reduces engagement
Capex intensity: High depreciation (Rs 126 Cr) suggests continued platform investment with unproven ROI
Valuation stretched: At 34.4x P/E with -4% TTM profit growth, the stock is overvalued for current trajectory
verdict_headline: Revenue-growing but profit-shrinking pharma tech platform: IPO hype has faded as margin pressures become evident; ROCE deterioration signals structural headwind
verdict_reasoning: Business has genuine niche (top-20 biopharma customer base) and secular tailwinds (life sciences digital transformation); justifies tracking on this list
But deep dive reveals critical operational stress: Q1 FY27 profit essentially flat (+0.17%) despite revenue +39.7%; TTM profit -4% vs revenue +30% indicates severe margin compression
ROCE deteriorated from 37% to 19% despite capex, suggesting capital deployment is becoming less efficient
Debtor days extended to 102 (vs 91 in FY24), signaling weaker customer quality or extended payment terms = working capital headwind
Valuation at 34.4x P/E is steep for -4% TTM profit growth; stock should trade 20-25x if profit growth remains stalled
Conviction on business = Medium (niche + tailwinds but structurally challenged by services commoditization); conviction on stock = HOLD/SELL at current levels
Revisit if: (i) Q2 FY27 results show profit re-acceleration (>10% growth), (ii) ROCE stabilizes at 22%+, (iii) Debtor days normalize to <95, (iv) Valuation compresses to 25x on normalized earnings

ROCE trend (red flag): FY20 not disclosed → FY21 55% (peak on low base) → FY22 46% → FY23 33% → FY24 29% → FY25 25% → FY26 19%; clear secular decline
OPM trend: FY20 -2% (loss) → FY26 18%; expanding but not fast enough to offset ROCE collapse
Capex / Investment: FY26 depreciation Rs 126 Cr (highest in history); capex intensity increasing for AI platform
Debtor days: FY24 91 days → FY26 102 days; extended receivables cycles = working capital headwind
quarterly_trend: Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026): revenue Rs 1,063 Cr (+39.7% YoY), OPM 16%, PAT Rs 116 Cr (+0.17% YoY) — CRITICAL: profit essentially flat despite 40% revenue growth
Previous quarters (Mar-Jun 2026): Q4 FY26 Rs 1,003 Cr, Q3 FY26 Rs 942 Cr, Q2 FY26 Rs 761 Cr; sequential acceleration evident but PAT has stalled
Margin compression visible: OPM 16% in Q1 FY27 vs 17-20% in prior year quarters; every point of OPM compression = Rs 10-15 Cr PAT impact at current scale
ASP trend unclear: Q1 revenue +39.7% but PAT +0.17% suggests either pricing pressure or delivery cost inflation

key_new_facts: Q1 FY27 profit growth completely stalled (+0.17%) despite revenue +39.7%; margin compression is structural, not cyclical
ROCE deteriorated from 37% (FY20) to 19% (FY26) — 50% decline despite capex; capital deployment efficiency is declining
Debtor days extended to 102 (from 91 in FY24); customer quality or payment terms weakening
Depreciation at Rs 126 Cr (highest ever) suggests continued heavy capex for AI platform with unproven ROI
TTM profit -4% vs revenue +30%; profit growth has completely diverged from revenue growth
open_questions: What is driving the Q1 FY27 profit stall? Pricing pressure, delivery cost inflation, mix shift to lower-margin services, or one-time charges?
When will profit growth re-accelerate? Is margin compression structural or cyclical?
What is the ROI on capex for AI platform investment (Rs 126 Cr depreciation FY26)?
Why did debtor days extend from 91 to 102? Customer quality issue or payment term extension?
What is the top customer concentration risk? Is top-3 customer revenue >30% of total?
deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium on the business (niche + tailwinds) but cautious on execution (profit momentum has stalled). Q2 FY27 results and concall (Oct 30, 2026) will be make-or-break for validating if margin compression is temporary or structural. If profit growth remains <5%, conviction drops to Medium-Low and stock is a SELL.
